why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1 and 2 hold: their cases are just examples of "limited to the range" and "throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi". Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its regex `'^#+ .*\\b'+n+'\\s*\\('` passes only if each function has a markdown heading in the form `name(`. The words "README.md documents every function" don't require that, so a README that documents the functions in a list or table would fail. That format rule belongs under Advisory. Check 4 also goes too far. "npm test passes" only needs a zero exit, but PASS also requires "the TAP summary shows `# fail 0`". The `node --test` spec reporter doesn't print that line, so a passing run could still fail the check.
